{"user":"I’m writing an academic email to my thesis supervisor asking for feedback on my draft chapter by next week. Can you draft a concise message I can send, and suggest a subject line?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a concise draft you can send, plus a few subject line options.

Subject line ideas:
1) Request for feedback on Chapter [#] draft (due next week)
2) Thesis Chapter [#] — feedback request
3) Chapter [#] draft: comments requested by next week

Email draft (concise):
Hi Prof. [Last Name],

I hope you’re doing well. I’m writing to ask whether you could provide feedback on my draft for Chapter [#], titled “[Chapter Title].]” If possible, I’d be grateful for your comments by next week so I can incorporate revisions.

I’ve attached the draft here: [file name]. Please let me know if you’d prefer specific sections in priority order.

Thank you very much for your time.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

Also, if you want, I can tailor this to your exact tone (more formal vs. more direct) and add one sentence summarizing what changed since your last review so the supervisor can give faster, more targeted feedback.","minus_response":"Subject line ideas:
1) Request for feedback on Chapter [#] draft
2) Chapter [#] draft — comments requested

Email draft:
Hi Prof. [Last Name],

I hope you’re doing well. Could I please get your feedback on my draft for Chapter [#] by next week? I’ve attached the document ([file name]).

Thank you,
[Your Name]

If you want, you can adjust the wording for formality, and you can pick whichever subject line you like. The rest is left as an exercise to you."}
